originalTitle: This is my new favorite laptop, but thanks to RAMageddon the price already went up by $800

content: Framework laptops always come with compromises in exchange for their unique DIY premise. Even though you pay extra for one compared to sleeker options from competitors, it’s easier to excuse minor flaws for modular ports, easy repairs, and an impressive range of upgradeable parts. So what happens when Framework goes “Pro”? We get a one-of-a-kind jewel among notebooks. The 13 Pro corrects and improves many shortcomings of the regular Laptop 13. It has a bright and sharp touchscreen, the best haptic trackpad not made by Apple, and an impeccable build and feel. Take all that and marry it to a great Intel chip and cutting-edge user-replaceable LPCAMM2 memory — both of which help to better balance performance and extra-long battery life — and you’ve got something really special. But what if this all happens in the throes of RAMageddon, with ever-increasing tech prices? Well, it’s now expensive as hell, of course. Our higher-end prebuilt review unit of the Laptop 13 Pro with a Windows license was meant to cost $2,299 when it arrived at my door, but after fresh memory price increases it’s now a nausea-inducing $3,099. An $800 price increase before reaching a single customer. We’ve seen lots of recent sticker shock, but this one especially hurts. [Product: Framework Laptop 13 Pro (Intel Core Ultra X7 358H) | https://framework.pxf.io/c/482924/1459308/17284?u=https%3A%2F%2Fframe.work%2Fproducts%2Flaptop13pro-intel-ultra-3%2Fconfiguration%2Fnew] --- Component report card * Screen: B * Webcam: B * Keyboard: A * Trackpad: A * Port selection: A * Speakers: C * Number of ugly stickers to remove: 1 on the Windows prebuilt (but only on the bottom) --- The Laptop 13 Pro is an all-black machine with an exquisite matte finish. It actually looks black instead of some variation of dark gray, and it feels rigid and well crafted — far from the hodgepodge erector set of its bigger cousin, the Laptop 16, or the good but slightly lower-quality build of the standard Laptop 13. Inside the 13 Pro are new Intel Panther Lake chips with LPCAMM2 RAM, or it can be optioned with last-gen AMD processors and slower SODIMM DDR5 memory. Our prebuilt review unit has a 16-core Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU with a 12-core Arc B390 integrated GPU, 32GB of RAM, 1TB SSD, and four modular USB-C ports. Unlike other Frameworks, each port supports Thunderbolt 4, DisplayPort 2.1, and up to 140W charging so you can freely mount your modular expansion cards without any restrictions. Everything here is really well put together. There’s no flex or give to the chassis or keyboard deck, even though everything’s easily disassembled with a handful of simple screws. The keyboard itself is great to type on. It maintains the nice 1.5mm key travel and tactility of the regular Laptop 13, but feels ever-so-slightly better thanks to a new one-piece aluminum frame. The 1080p webcam is a holdover from the regular model, maintaining its solid performance — it’s pretty sharp, if just a touch grainy in some lighting. The big upgrades to the 13 Pro’s components are the new haptic trackpad and touchscreen LCD. This is the best non-Apple haptic trackpad I’ve ever used. It’s very responsive to “clicks” from corner to corner, and it feels and sounds just right. The new screen is still a 13.5-inch matte-finish 120Hz IPS panel with 2880 x 1920 resolution for that excellent 3:2 aspect ratio, but it’s brighter (700 nits) and touch-enabled. Until now, a touchscreen on a Framework was only found on the cheaper Laptop 12. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268670_Framework_Laptop_13_Pro_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0001.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268670_Framework_Laptop_13_Pro_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0002.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268670_Framework_Laptop_13_Pro_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0006.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/07/268670_Framework_Laptop_13_Pro_laptop_review_ADiBenedetto_0008.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] The 13 Pro’s audio comes from a pair of side-firing stereo speakers. The speakers were one of the weaker points of the standard Laptop 13, and they’re the 13 Pro’s biggest fault. The side-mounted orientation creates a tiny bit of a soundstage, but overall the speakers sound a little thin and treble-y with minimal bass. When I reviewed the Laptop 13, a savvy commenter pointed me toward open-source app FxSound to help with its audio woes. FxSound does help the 13 Pro sound noticeably better and fuller (with lots of EQ and boost options), but unfortunately for Linux users it’s Windows only. The Intel chip and LPCAMM2 memory inside do a great job delivering on both performance and exceptional power efficiency. This newer style of compression-mounted memory is better for both of those factors, just like LPDDR5X, but without having to be soldered to the main board. The tradeoff for using LPCAMM2 is that it’s newer tech that’s generally pricier than DDR5 (gulp). chineseContent: 架构笔记本电脑总是会做出妥协，以换取其独特的 DIY 前提。尽管与竞争对手的更时尚的选择相比，您需要支付额外的费用，但模块化端口、易于维修和一系列令人印象深刻的可升级部件的小缺陷更容易被原谅。那么当 Framework 变成“Pro”时会发生什么呢？我们得到了笔记本中独一无二的宝石。 13 Pro 纠正并改进了普通笔记本电脑 13 的许多缺点。它拥有明亮锐利的触摸屏、非苹果制造的最好的触觉触控板，以及无可挑剔的构造和手感。将这一切与出色的英特尔芯片和尖端的用户可更换 LPCAMM2 内存结合起来——这两者都有助于更好地平衡性能和超长的电池寿命——你就得到了一些真正特别的东西。但如果这一切都发生在拉米吉登的痛苦之中，科技价格不断上涨怎么办？好吧，当然，现在它太贵了。我们的高端预装笔记本电脑 13 Pro 具有 Windows 许可证，当它到达我家门口时，原价为 2,299 美元，但在新内存价格上涨后，现在价格为 3,099 美元，令人恶心。在到达单个客户之前价格上涨 800 美元。我们最近看到了很多令人震惊的标价，但这次尤其令人痛心。 [产品：框架笔记本电脑 13 Pro (Intel Core Ultra X7 358H) | https://framework.pxf.io/c/482924/1459308/17284?u=https%3A%2F%2Fframe.work%2Fproducts%2Flaptop13pro-intel-ultra-3%2Fconfiguration%2Fnew] --- 组件报告卡 * 屏幕：B * 网络摄像头：B * 键盘：A * 触控板：A * 端口选择：A * 扬声器：C * 丑数要去除的贴纸： 1 在 Windows 预装上（但仅在底部） --- Laptop 13 Pro 是一款全黑机器，具有精致的哑光饰面。它实际上看起来是黑色的，而不是深灰色的某种变体，
